statement: Iraq’s projected water deficit is driven jointly by demand growth, upstream withdrawals and dams, domestic management, pollution and climate pressures; a 2026 World Bank concept diagnostic projects a 10.9 billion m3 demand-supply gap by 2035.
compact_statement: Demand growth, upstream withdrawals, domestic management, pollution and climate pressures jointly drive Iraq’s water deficit; the projected 2035 gap is 10.9 billion m3.

source_refs.locator: Sectoral and Institutional Context, PDF pp. 3-4; 2035 gap and interacting drivers.

uncertainty: The World Bank concept diagnostic synthesizes sector evidence and does not apportion the projected deficit among climate, upstream and domestic drivers.

statement: As of September 2025, a UN synthesis reported 31,001 families (186,006 people) displaced due to climatic factors in central and southern Iraq; 63% had moved from rural to urban areas.
compact_statement: As of September 2025, 186,006 people were reported displaced by climatic factors in central and southern Iraq; 63% had moved from rural to urban areas.

source_refs.locator: publication text, para. beginning “Water scarcity has had…”. (The United Nations in Iraq)

uncertainty: UN advocacy synthesis; underlying DTM instrument was not independently reproduced here; “climatic factors” is broader than anthropogenic climate attribution.

statement: A 2026 World Bank diagnostic reports 83% access to improved drinking-water sources in 2023 but only 60% of households reporting safe and consistently available water; non-revenue water exceeds 60%, sewerage coverage is below 30%, and over 70% of urban sewage is discharged untreated.
compact_statement: Water-service weakness compounds climate exposure.

source_refs.locator: §Sectoral and Institutional Context, para.6, PDF p.4.

uncertainty: Sector diagnostic aggregates heterogeneous regional conditions.

statement: World Bank modeling estimates 35% of agriculture and construction workers are exposed to extreme heat, with productivity and earnings implications.
compact_statement: Outdoor and manual workers face substantial heat exposure.

source_refs.locator: Special Focus, Fig.19 discussion, PDF p.31. (World Bank)

uncertainty: Model/synthesis estimate; not an occupational cohort evaluation.

statement: World Bank modeling finds a 20% decline in water availability plus higher-temperature crop impacts could reduce medium-term GDP by 3.9%; modeled 10-20% food-price rises would increase poverty by 1.6-4.4 percentage points.
compact_statement: Climate-water-agriculture shocks can transmit through prices and poverty.

source_refs.locator: Special Focus, Fig.19 discussion, PDF p.31. (World Bank)

uncertainty: Scenario modeling, not observed outcome or causal estimate of conflict.

statement: Iraq's 2025 NDC explicitly calls for meaningful participation by vulnerable communities, youth, women and persons with disabilities and notes disproportionate climate impacts on women and vulnerable rural/ecosystem-dependent populations.
compact_statement: National policy recognizes differentiated vulnerability.

source_refs.locator: PDF p.8 and §Women, Girls and Vulnerable Groups, pp.35-36.

uncertainty: Mostly policy diagnosis; quantitative comparative impact evidence is limited and some statistics require independent validation.

statement: The 2025 NDC calls for Ministry of Environment-Ministry of Planning co-leadership, stronger National Climate Committee capacity and establishment of an NDC implementation unit with workplans, indicators and data systems.
compact_statement: Iraq has a defined national climate-governance architecture.

source_refs.locator: §Institutional Arrangement for Implementation, PDF pp.37-38.

uncertainty: Existence/planned strengthening of architecture does not demonstrate implementation quality or outcomes.

statement: The Kurdistan Region's 2024 LAP was developed through a participatory technical-working-group process and specifies a future monitoring, review and learning structure with indicators, data collection and periodic evaluation.
compact_statement: KRI has localized adaptation planning and proposed MRL capacity.

source_refs.locator: Executive Summary pp.9-10; MRL pp.12-13.

uncertainty: Plan-level capacity only; not evidence of achieved resilience; KRI findings cannot be generalized nationally.

statement: World Bank modeling indicates that improving water-use efficiency by 10% or 20% would reduce the modeled GDP loss from the water/temperature shock scenario from 3.9% to 3.1% or 2.4%, respectively.
compact_statement: Water efficiency has modeled adaptation benefits.

source_refs.locator: Special Focus, PDF p.31. (World Bank)

uncertainty: Modeled benefit, not evaluated implementation performance.

statement: The approved USD 39 million SRVALI programme is designed for six years in Karbala, Muthanna and Najaf to improve climate-resilient agriculture and water-use efficiency, with close to two million intended rural beneficiaries.
compact_statement: A major targeted adaptation investment is planned in three governorates.

source_refs.locator: paras.7-14 and 22-32. (The United Nations in Iraq)

uncertainty: Financing/design verified; beneficiary and resilience statements are targets, not measured outcomes.

statement: WFP's independent evaluation found unconditional food assistance buffered shocks for vulnerable IDPs/refugees, while ongoing shocks and soaring prices partly offset food-security gains; difficulties demonstrating results and lack of a collective social-protection vision weakened sustainability of newer initiatives.
compact_statement: WFP assistance buffered shocks but sustainability/results evidence was limited.

source_refs.locator: official evaluation page, conclusions bullets. (World Food Programme)

uncertainty: Only official evaluation-page summary was accessible; not specifically a climate-program evaluation.

statement: UNDP's independent evaluation found climate/clean-energy elements within stabilization activities were mostly ad hoc and piecemeal, while critical-infrastructure rehabilitation was delivered at substantial scale and was perceived as facilitating return and strengthening the social contract.
compact_statement: Stabilization delivered infrastructure, but climate integration was weakly systematic.

source_refs.locator: Finding 6, PDF pp.22-24.

uncertainty: Independent evaluation, but climate-specific activities were a small part of the evaluated portfolio.

statement: UNAMI states that climate change does not directly cause conflict; hazards can exacerbate tensions where social, economic and political conditions, grievances and poor resource management create pathways to insecurity.
compact_statement: Climate is a risk multiplier, not a deterministic conflict cause.

source_refs.locator: Introduction, PDF p.5.

uncertainty: Strong causal calibration but primarily qualitative synthesis, not causal identification.

statement: UNAMI reports that environmentally/climate-displaced people commonly move to urban centres with limited services and employment, and documents exclusion and harassment that can increase inter-community tensions.
compact_statement: Displacement can transmit climate stress into urban service and cohesion pressures.

source_refs.locator: Existing analysis, PDF pp.6-7; displacement section pp.12-13.

uncertainty: Relies partly on IOM/Berghof evidence and qualitative cases; conflict consequence is conditional.

statement: In March 2024, a water-access dispute in southeastern Dhi Qar escalated violently, causing fatalities and injuries and requiring national security intervention; UNAMI emphasizes that weapons and political/armed-group affiliations complicate such conflicts.
compact_statement: Water competition has produced localized violence, but climate is only one contributor.

source_refs.locator: §Natural resource competition, PDF pp.9-10.

uncertainty: Direct violence observed; complete climate -> violence causal chain is not isolated. Must not be generalized nationally.

statement: UNAMI documents instances where armed groups or affiliates bypass or impede land, water and service regulation, potentially undermining water security, public services and climate adaptation.
compact_statement: Armed-actor political economy can obstruct adaptation.
ecological_level: Muthanna; Missan; Basra and other cited locations

source_refs.locator: §Exploitation of natural resources by armed actors, PDF pp.11-12.

uncertainty: Qualitative/report-based cases; degree of representativeness is unknown.

statement: UNAMI finds that inconsistent assistance and unclear registration/responsibility for climate-displaced people can generate perceived neglect and distrust, with politically contingent assistance leaving people vulnerable to manipulation.
compact_statement: Assistance gaps can turn displacement into a governance/social-cohesion risk.

source_refs.locator: §Limited and politically-motivated assistance for climate displacement, PDF pp.12-14.

uncertainty: Qualitative and partly case-specific; “climate displaced” classification can include environmental factors beyond attribution to climate change.

statement: In Al-Rifai, Berghof respondents reported that water-access conflicts had subsided in a wetter year and that, when disputes occurred, tribal, security and administrative authorities generally resolved them quickly.
compact_statement: Local institutions can contain water-related disputes.

source_refs.locator: Al-Rifai district findings, PDF pp.21-22.

uncertainty: Self-reported local perceptions; cannot establish a general national coping capacity.

statement: UNAMI identifies participatory climate and natural-resource governance as a potential peace-supporting capacity and cites the May 2024 Kirkuk Climate Forum as an example of climate issues creating space for dialogue and collective action.
compact_statement: Inclusive climate governance can create peace-supporting dialogue opportunities.

source_refs.locator: recommendations/conclusion, PDF pp.16-18.

uncertainty: Evidence supports an entry point/opportunity, not a quantified reduction in violence.

statement: In the March–April 2022 returnee survey, nearly 75% of surveyed farming households reported lower harvests than in 2014; over 80% of livestock owners reported smaller herds.
compact_statement: In the March–April 2022 returnee survey, nearly 75% of surveyed farming households reported lower harvests than in 2014; over 80% of livestock owners reported smaller herds.
geographies: 14 districts of return: Mosul, Ramadi, Falluja, Telafar, Tikrit, Heet, Hawija, Hamdaniya, Shirqat, Kirkuk, Baiji, Sinjar, Khanaqin and Balad

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 3, farming and livestock production findings

uncertainty: Self-reported; multiple drivers discussed. Historical 2022 responses, not a 2026 assessment.

statement: In the March–April 2022 returnee survey, ISIL-era conflict destroyed farm assets and infrastructure; limited replacement capacity and incentives hindered agricultural recovery.
compact_statement: In the March–April 2022 returnee survey, ISIL-era conflict destroyed farm assets and infrastructure; limited replacement capacity and incentives hindered agricultural recovery.
geographies: Districts of return in Anbar, Diyala, Kirkuk, Ninewa and Salah al-Din

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 2 and 4, conflict and agricultural recovery

uncertainty: Multiple barriers; relative effects not isolated. Historical 2022 responses, not a 2026 assessment.

statement: The 2022 returnee survey describes stronger weather sensitivity in Sinjar, Shirqat, Hamdaniya and Telafar. Across the sample, about a quarter of farming abandonments cited water scarcity and about a tenth unpredictable weather; costs and conflict losses also mattered.
compact_statement: The 2022 returnee survey describes stronger weather sensitivity in Sinjar, Shirqat, Hamdaniya and Telafar. Across the sample, about a quarter of farming abandonments cited water scarcity and about a tenth unpredictable weather; costs and conflict losses also mattered.
geographies: Northern districts including Sinjar, Shirqat, Hamdaniya and Telafar

source_refs.locator: One-based PDF p.7, district variation and agricultural-abandonment discussion.

uncertainty: Respondent attributions; economic and conflict factors also mattered. Historical 2022 responses, not a 2026 assessment.

statement: The 2024 portal-published IOM brief recommends early warning, technology and broader agricultural investment to support durable returns; these are proposals, not evaluated adaptation results.
compact_statement: The 2024 portal-published IOM brief recommends early warning, technology and broader agricultural investment to support durable returns; these are proposals, not evaluated adaptation results.

source_refs.locator: One-based PDF p.9, Implications for sustainable reintegration.

uncertainty: Proposal, not evaluated. Historical 2022 responses, not a 2026 assessment.

statement: NRC's 2024 publisher summary reports: In the 2024 farming season, 57% of surveyed returnee households used less land or water; 5% reported being forced to move because of drought conditions.
compact_statement: NRC's 2024 publisher summary reports: In the 2024 farming season, 57% of surveyed returnee households used less land or water; 5% reported being forced to move because of drought conditions.

source_refs.locator: Publisher summary, returnee households

uncertainty: Publisher summary only; questionnaire, denominator and detailed methods were not available in the inspected page. These are 2024 survey findings, not current 2026 prevalence.

statement: NRC's 2024 publisher summary reports: Among displaced households in informal sites, one in five lacked clean water, three quarters reported water-sharing tensions, and 44% said authorities barred some groups from water.
compact_statement: NRC's 2024 publisher summary reports: Among displaced households in informal sites, one in five lacked clean water, three quarters reported water-sharing tensions, and 44% said authorities barred some groups from water.

source_refs.locator: Publisher summary, displaced households in informal sites

uncertainty: Publisher summary only; results are not disaggregated further in the accessible excerpt. These are 2024 survey findings, not current 2026 prevalence.

statement: NRC's 2024 publisher summary reports: The report says four in five displaced respondents linked return decisions to the ability to farm, and 93% based stay, move or return decisions on information about local resources.
compact_statement: NRC's 2024 publisher summary reports: The report says four in five displaced respondents linked return decisions to the ability to farm, and 93% based stay, move or return decisions on information about local resources.
geographies: Displacement sites in Anbar, Duhok, Ninewa and Salah al-Din

source_refs.locator: Publisher summary, return decisions

uncertainty: Publisher summary only; do not interpret stated decision factors as observed return outcomes. These are 2024 survey findings, not current 2026 prevalence.

statement: Across 294 subdistricts from 2020-2022, the study reports a direct association between skin temperature and battle events, with soil moisture and energy operating indirectly.
compact_statement: Across 294 subdistricts from 2020-2022, the study reports a direct association between skin temperature and battle events, with soil moisture and energy operating indirectly.

source_refs.locator: Abstract and results, environmental variables and battle events

uncertainty: Observational model; authors note omitted social and political variables and limited temporal specificity.

statement: Population density positively mediated modeled conflict activity, while wheat production did not reduce conflict as hypothesized.
compact_statement: Population density positively mediated modeled conflict activity, while wheat production did not reduce conflict as hypothesized.

source_refs.locator: Results and limitations

uncertainty: Model result is limited by omitted social-political variables and the 2020-2022 period.

statement: Participants described drought, reduced rainfall and water scarcity as undermining farming and increasing irrigation and land competition, including farmer-herder tension in rural Nimrud and Hatra.
compact_statement: Participants described drought, reduced rainfall and water scarcity as undermining farming and increasing irrigation and land competition, including farmer-herder tension in rural Nimrud and Hatra.

source_refs.locator: One-based PDF p.11, section3.4 Climate Stress and Resource Tension.

uncertainty: Qualitative perceptions from purposive February 2026 fieldwork; not a representative estimate.

statement: Participants reported that women, youth, people with disabilities, low-income households and displaced or returnee groups face unequal access to land, capital, irrigation and employment in parts of Ninewa.
compact_statement: Participants reported that women, youth, people with disabilities, low-income households and displaced or returnee groups face unequal access to land, capital, irrigation and employment in parts of Ninewa.

source_refs.locator: One-based PDF p.12, section3.5 Exclusion and Vulnerability Patterns.

uncertainty: Reported qualitative access barriers; the assessment does not estimate prevalence.

statement: The assessment identifies tribal mediation, kinship networks, shared economic activity and community initiatives as local peace capacities, while noting exclusion of less-connected groups.
compact_statement: The assessment identifies tribal mediation, kinship networks, shared economic activity and community initiatives as local peace capacities, while noting exclusion of less-connected groups.

source_refs.locator: One-based PDF pp.13 and16, actors/local influence and Connectors and Local Capacities for Peace.

uncertainty: Qualitative assessment; capacities are described, not impact-evaluated.
